Designed and produced by Maxim Transport Industries beginning in 2689, the Maxim Heavy Hover Transport was the brainchild of a retired infantry general on Al Na'ir who envisioned a single vehicle capable of delivering an entire infantry platoon to the battlefield. Before the Maxim, commanders relied on lances of three or four smaller APCs to deploy a single platoon, a logistically cumbersome arrangement that limited tactical flexibility.

The Maxim proved an immediate success across the Inner Sphere, earning a reputation as the gold standard for military hover transports. Popular with commanders for its combination of speed, firepower, and carrying capacity, the Maxim is equally respected by the infantry who ride in its spacious and comfortable bay. Though Maxim Transport Industries itself is long gone, the design endures through multiple successor manufacturers, evidence of the soundness of the original concept.

The Maxim mounts an impressive weapons array for a transport vehicle. A turret-mounted SureShot Mk VI SRM-6 serves as the primary close-range weapon, supplemented by side-mounted SureShot II SRM-2 launchers. Three LongFire V LRM-5 racks provide sustained long-range fire support, with two forward-facing and one rear-mounted to cover withdrawals. A trio of heavy machine guns in the turret rounds out the armament, giving the Maxim effective anti-infantry capability during troop deployment.

Powered by a PowerTech 165 Highlift internal combustion engine, the Maxim reaches a top speed of 129 kilometers per hour. Five and a half tons of ArcShield V armor provide adequate protection for its weight class, though the hover skirt remains a persistent vulnerability to concentrated fire. The six-ton infantry bay accommodates a full platoon with padded seating and enough space for troops to check weapons and move comfortably. This combination of firepower and carrying capacity makes the Maxim far more capable than a simple transport, though commanders must weigh its combat value against the risk of losing an entire platoon in a single vehicle.

Maxim Transport Industries was founded on Al Na'ir as a startup led by a retired infantry general who understood firsthand the limitations of existing troop transports. When the Maxim entered service in 2689, it was the first hover vehicle capable of carrying a full infantry platoon in a single chassis. The design's unexpected success allowed MTI to expand rapidly, opening additional production facilities on Skye and Sian. The company had plans for further expansion to Atreus and Kathil, though these facilities were never realized.

Despite the Maxim's commercial triumph, MTI's subsequent attempts to diversify into other military products proved to be dismal failures and a significant drain on profitability. The company limped along for centuries on the strength of its sole successful product. In 3037, a massive scandal erupted within MTI involving accusations of embezzlement, inappropriate conduct between coworkers, and rumors of bizarre hazing rituals. The scandal proved fatal, and MTI was dissolved.

Prominent corporations moved quickly to acquire the defunct company's assets. Scarborough Manufacturers purchased the original MTI plant on Al Na'ir, while Cyclops Incorporated absorbed the Skye facility. The Sian plant saw the most dramatic transition when Hellespont Industrials seized control with an armed force. Commander Max Cooper, the guard commander at the Sian facility and a significant MTI shareholder, attempted to hold the plant by force during the dissolution. His troops, composed of infantrymen and their Maxim transports, held the facility for twelve hours before Hellespont's corporate militia overwhelmed the defenders. Cooper's forces retreated and attempted a second assault hours later, but the swift hovertanks were no match for the now-entrenched Hellespont defenders. Cooper lost his life in the failed counterattack.

Under their new owners, Maxim production continued without interruption. Each manufacturer maintained the original design specifications, ensuring parts compatibility across the Inner Sphere. The Maxim remained the standard infantry transport through the Late Succession Wars and into the technological renaissance that followed the discovery of the Helm Memory Core. Scarborough Manufacturers introduced the first major upgrade in 3052, integrating Streak missile technology, ferro-fibrous armor, and a TAG system into the proven chassis. The upgrade program brought modern capabilities to the venerable design while preserving the reliable foundation that had served for over three centuries.

During the FedCom Civil War, Maxim-equipped infantry forces saw extensive action across multiple theaters. A common tactic saw Maxim platoons establish perimeters under heavy fire, deploy their infantry, and then fall back to provide long-range fire support until the infantry required extraction. In Free Worlds League space, Capellan soldiers used a company of Maxims to flank a combined-arms force during a raid on a Sirius-system world, routing the defenders when massed LRM fire spooked the raiders into retreating. The concentrated SRM fire from the Maxim formation crippled one BattleMech at a time as the panicked raiders fled the system.

The rise of battle armor across the Inner Sphere created new challenges and opportunities for the Maxim. Both factory and field modifications emerged to accommodate the heavier, bulkier battle armor suits, while other variants optimized the chassis for electronic warfare and networked combat. Production continued across all three successor manufacturers through the Jihad, the Republic era, and into the ilClan period, with the Maxim remaining one of the most widely fielded hover transports in human-occupied space.

Before the Maxim, commanders relied on lances of three or four smaller APCs to deploy a single platoon, a logistically cumbersome arrangement that limited tactical flexibility.

The Maxim proved an immediate success across the Inner Sphere, earning a reputation as the gold standard for military hover transports. Popular with commanders for its combination of speed, firepower, and carrying capacity, the Maxim is equally respected by the infantry who ride in its spacious and comfortable bay. Though Maxim Transport Industries itself is long gone, the design endures through multiple successor manufacturers, proof of the soundness of the original concept.

The Mk II's spacious sixteen-ton infantry bay is its defining feature, capable of carrying a full platoon of battle armor or an entire company of conventional infantry. Adjustable handholds and equipment hooks line the walls, while storage bins offer space for ammunition, power packs, and other combat essentials. Multifunction fold-down stations accommodate both standard power armor and quad suits, with a quick release system for rapid egress.

A pair of Helga Series three-tube Multi-Missile Launchers provide the sole offensive armament, mounted in the turret. Though light by Maxim standards, the MML-3s offer tactical flexibility through their ability to fire standard LRM or SRM loads as well as specialty munitions like Thunder LRM mines. Two tons of ammunition stored in a CASE-protected bin ensure the crew and passengers survive any catastrophic detonation. Five and a half tons of ArcShield Heavy ferro-fibrous armor provide above-average protection for the weight class. The PowerTech 165 Highlifter fusion engine maintains the traditional Maxim top speed of 129 kilometers per hour while eliminating the logistical burden of fuel resupply. The primary drawback is the near total reliance on embarked troops for close defense once the infantry has deployed.

The Maxim Mk II emerged from the Republic Armed Forces' "Anyone Can Be a Hero" recruiting campaign, which dramatically expanded the need for heavy infantry carriers capable of deploying battle armor in large numbers. Both Cyclops Industries and Scarborough Manufacturers submitted competing proposals, each drawing on their decades of experience producing the original Maxim. When the RAF selected the Maxim as the basis for their new transport, neither company could independently meet the production requirements or the RAF's demanding specifications.

Scarborough approached Cyclops with a joint venture proposal, but the partnership proved contentious from the start. Heated debates erupted over the appropriate battlefield role for the Mk II. Amidst significant media coverage, Cyclops's executive VP of development, Shiloh Connolly, resigned over the direction of the project. Connolly publicly stated that the final specifications ignored the Maxim's lengthy and successful history of combat support roles, producing a vehicle designed to avoid fights rather than win them. Scarborough's engineers countered that reducing the weapons load would keep the Mk II out of combat and extend its service life, allowing the RAF to invest more in battle armor and other equipment. The RAF ultimately sided with Scarborough's philosophy, and the Maxim Mk II entered production in 3083.

The entire first production run went to the regiments of the Hastati Sentinels. Subsequent runs were divided between the Sentinels, Triarii Protectors, and Principes Guards, with approximately ninety percent being the standard configuration. The RAF standard procedure called for each Mk II to transport a full platoon of battle armor, though additional configurations could accommodate two motorized infantry platoons, four platoons of jump infantry, or five platoons of conventional foot soldiers. Multi-role loadouts typically included two squads of battle armor alongside two platoons of jump or foot infantry.

The Mk II Infantry Support variant, produced exclusively on Skye and known colloquially as the "Shiloh" after the departed Cyclops executive, addressed the concerns Connolly had raised. By halving the infantry bay and installing light PPCs and machine guns, the Shiloh provided substantially more organic firepower. The variant was exported to the Lyran Commonwealth, where it was assigned to units in the Bolan and Donegal provinces. Beginning in 3088, the RAF also deployed standard Mk IIs to prefecture militias, expanding the vehicle's presence throughout Republic territory.

Production at both the Skye and Al Na'ir facilities continued through the Republic era and into the Dark Age. When Clan Jade Falcon seized Skye, the Cyclops facility fell under Falcon control, though production of the Mk II continued for the new owners. Following the formation of the ilClan, the Skye plant transferred to Clan Wolf Empire authority. The Al Na'ir facility passed through Word of Blake control during the Jihad, then Republic of the Sphere governance, before returning to Draconis Combine ownership as the Republic contracted. Both plants remain active producers of the Mk II through the current era, ensuring the design continues to serve multiple successor states simultaneously.

The ECM variant emerged as a field modification in 3087, downgrading the turret weaponry to a single Streak SRM-2 while adding a Guardian ECM suite. This configuration proved popular with units operating in electronic warfare environments, where the ECM protection offset the reduced firepower. The full infantry bay was retained, maintaining the Mk II's primary transport mission while adding a valuable force-multiplier capability to the formation.

Named for the Hebrew word meaning "chariot," the Merkava was Leopard Armor's signature heavy tank and the primary armored vehicle of the Terran Alliance and its successor state, the Terran Hegemony. The original design entered service with the Alliance in 2294, and a succession of upgraded marks followed over the next two centuries. Each iteration built upon the tank's reputation for rugged construction and ease of field maintenance. The Merkava became a symbol of Hegemony military power during the Age of War, serving on dozens of fronts across known space. Its lineage influenced subsequent heavy tank designs for centuries, with vehicles such as the Manticore and Von Luckner drawing upon battlefield lessons learned by Merkava crews.

The Merkava is a turret-based heavy tank designed around a balanced mix of direct fire and missile support. In its definitive Mk. VIII configuration, the tank mounts a Class 5 Armstrong autocannon as its primary weapon, supplemented by a Harpoon-15 long-range missile launcher for indirect fire support. A Harpoon-4 short-range missile launcher provides close-range punch, while a pair of M-3 machine guns handle anti-infantry duties, one mounted in the turret and the other on the hull front. The Vlar 300 fusion engine gives the 75-ton tank a respectable top speed of 64 kph, a significant improvement over the 54 kph achieved by earlier ICE and primitive fusion variants.

Ten tons of PanzerSlab armor provide solid protection across all facings, with near-even distribution between hull and turret. The Merkava's chief weakness was its inability to evolve alongside increasingly powerful weapons technology. Even the fusion-powered marks carried armament considered outdated by the late Star League era. Earlier variants suffered additional drawbacks, including the fuel dependency of internal combustion engines and the substandard protection of primitive armor that proved especially vulnerable to energy weapons.

The Merkava's history spans nearly eight centuries, from its debut with the Terran Alliance in 2294 through its revival during the Jihad. Leopard Armor of Terra produced the original design as a mainstay battle tank for Alliance ground forces. As the Alliance evolved into the Terran Hegemony, the tank was continually upgraded. The Mk. VI, introduced in 2384, became the standard heavy tank of the Hegemony Armed Forces during the turbulent Age of War. To the general public, the Merkava symbolized Hegemony military power as much as the mighty WarShips of the Hegemony Navy, earning it the nickname "King of the Battlefield."

The ICE-powered Merkavas earned their reputation across numerous campaigns, but operational limitations became apparent as the Hegemony expanded its borders. During a six-month campaign to wrest control of Kentares IV from Federated Suns forces in 2431, the constraints of combustion-powered vehicles were painfully exposed. The Hegemony responded by commissioning the Mk. VII in 2435, the first Merkava to mount a fusion engine. The new mark proved itself during the Battle of Tybalt, where it helped secure the world as a Hegemony protectorate against Capellan opposition.

By 2439, the older Mk. VI had been relegated to militia duties and training roles. Four of these obsolescent tanks were stripped of their LRM launchers, fitted with remote-control systems, and pressed into service as target drones for a secret weapons test at the Yakima firing range on Terra. On February 5th of that year, Colonel Charles Kincaid piloted the prototype Mackie BattleMech against the four remotely operated Merkavas and destroyed all of them without sustaining any damage. The brutal efficiency of the demonstration stunned observers and cemented the BattleMech's place as the dominant weapon of ground warfare. The tank once celebrated as the "King of the Battlefield" had helped usher in its own replacement.

The Mk. VIII entered service in 2465 with a more refined fusion engine derived from BattleMech research, and it served the Hegemony Armed Forces through the Reunification War. Leopard Armor discontinued Merkava production in 2601, judging that further modifications could not keep pace with advancing technology. Surviving Mk. VIIIs were transferred to militia formations or sold to Star League member states. By the fall of the Star League, few remained intact, and those that did were cannibalized for their valuable fusion engines during the Succession Wars.

The Merkava might have remained a historical footnote if not for the discovery of the Hegemony Memory Core. During the Jihad, Earthwerks Incorporated recognized the tank's simple construction as an advantage for rapid wartime production. The company established a makeshift manufacturing facility on Tiber in the Principality of Regulus and began producing the modernized Mk. IX. By 3073, the Regulan Hussars were receiving the new tanks in large numbers, giving the ancient Merkava lineage an unexpected second life.

The Minion Advanced Tactical Vehicle is a 20-ton hovercraft developed through an unusual joint venture between General Motors of Kathil and Ceres Metals Industries of Tikonov, linking manufacturers from the Federated Suns and Capellan Confederation under the political umbrella of the Federated Commonwealth. Conceived around 3061 as an open-battlefield strike vehicle, its commercial rollout was delayed by uncertainty surrounding the Clan threat. The outbreak of the FedCom Civil War revived demand almost immediately, and the design was adapted to serve a dedicated urban combat role alongside the larger Morningstar City Command Vehicle.

The Minion's integration with C³ Command/Control/Communications networks defines its battlefield purpose. Built from the outset to serve as a network node rather than a standalone combatant, it fills a niche in combined-arms formations for both Federated Suns and Capellan Confederation forces.

The Minion's Nissan 95 fusion powerplant gives it a top speed exceeding 150 kph, placing it among the faster combat vehicles in its weight class. Its five and a half tons of Durallex Light armor provide meaningful protection for a hovercraft, allowing it to absorb punishment while continuing to maneuver. The primary armament of two Defiance P5M Medium Pulse Lasers delivers accurate, sustained fire at close to medium range, with the pulse mechanism compensating for the minor targeting fluctuations inherent to high-speed hover movement.

On open streets and flat terrain, the Minion's exceptional speed forces opponents to track its movement while its pulse weapons strip armor. In urban environments, however, narrow streets and blocked intersections can severely restrict this tactical flexibility, which is the design's most significant operational limitation.

The Brightstar 17 Mk. II targeting system was developed specifically for use with pulse lasers and integrates with a C³ slave unit, linking the Minion to a broader Command/Control/Communications network. This connectivity is the vehicle's defining tactical asset. The Minion feeds targeting data to friendly units across the battlefield, functioning as a mobile sensor node that multiplies the effectiveness of the entire formation rather than simply contributing its own firepower.

The Minion originated as a joint development project made possible by the political integration of the Federated Commonwealth. General Motors of Kathil and Ceres Metals Industries of Tikonov collaborated on the design beginning around 3061, with both manufacturers contributing to the tooling and production architecture. Initial sales projections were dampened when uncertainty surrounding the ongoing Clan threat slowed procurement interest across the Inner Sphere.

The FedCom Civil War proved to be the design's commercial salvation. As fighting engulfed Kathil, local commanders identified a pressing need for fast, network-capable urban combatants that could integrate into Command/Control/Communications nets alongside BattleMechs. The Minion was rapidly adapted to this role, pairing with the Morningstar in a dedicated city-support team configuration. Katherine Steiner-Davion's loyalists were among the first to deploy Minions from the Kathil production runs, using them during the fighting on Kathil and Tikonov. By late 3065, Victor Steiner-Davion's forces had seized control of both facilities, turning the design against its previous operators. The Minion saw particularly intense use during the assault on New Avalon.

The Tikonov facility's proximity to Capellan space created political complications. Despite a Federated Suns prohibition on military technology transfers, production notes were shared with a Ceres Metals facility on Warlock, enabling a second Capellan production line. When Capellan forces retook Tikonov during the later civil war period, they reassigned the Tikonov output to their own formations and began retooling the nearby Warlock plant for additional production. The Tikonov facility passed through independent and then Republic of the Sphere control during the Jihad and early Dark Age before eventually returning to Capellan ownership. The Kathil line remained under Federated Suns control throughout, sustaining steady production into the ilClan era.

The Mithras Light Tank is a Clan combat vehicle designed to serve as both a swift cavalry unit and a versatile fire support platform. Developed by Clan scientists in the mid-twenty-ninth century, the design emerged as a practical answer to the need for fast, hard-hitting light armor capable of engaging targets across multiple range brackets. The Mithras occupies a well-established niche in Clan vehicle doctrine, operating as a quick-response unit equally suited to harrying flanks, supporting Elemental assaults, or sustaining pressure on retreating forces. Though its thin armor limits staying power in sustained engagements, the design's combination of speed and weapons flexibility has made it a reliable fixture across multiple Clans throughout the Succession Wars era and beyond.

The Mithras is operated by a two-man crew. The driver manages vehicle movement and sensor operations, while the gunner handles the weapons and communication systems using an integrated Combined Weapon System. The CWS allows both turret weapons to be aimed and fired simultaneously, a significant tactical advantage. The absence of a secondary gun sight means the front-mounted laser cannot be fired if the vehicle's sensors are disabled, reducing the gunner's options when the CWS becomes inoperative.

The primary weapon is a Type 25 Ultra Autocannon/2 mounted in the turret for full arc coverage. Its advanced autoloader allows variable rates of fire, up to twelve rounds per minute at full speed. The recoil mechanism is prone to fouling the autoloader track, however, which can jam the system and render the gun useless at critical moments. Two Series 2b Extended Range Medium Lasers complement the cannon. One is mounted coaxially in the turret to cover the autocannon's dead zone, while the second is fixed in the hull front for suppression when the turret is engaged elsewhere.

The Mithras carries only three tons of armor, but the Compound Alpha Ferro-Fibrous construction provides protection equivalent to more than four tons of standard plating. The vehicle can absorb hits from all but the largest weapons as a result. The rear armor is the design's primary weakness, as a single hit from even a light or medium weapon can breach it, leaving the vehicle vulnerable to catastrophic damage from behind.

The Mithras traces its origins to the early decades of Clan society, when Clan scientists worked to provide their ground forces with a fast, adaptable tracked vehicle suited to the varied terrain of the Clan homeworlds. Introduced in 2845 during the Early Succession Wars period, the design drew on the lessons of the Pentagon Civil Wars and the Clans' subsequent drive to standardize their military equipment. The Mithras emerged as a pragmatic light cavalry platform, filling the gap between heavier tanks and the purely Elemental-focused ground warfare doctrine that many Clans preferred.

During the early homeworld era, Clan Ice Hellion operated a production line at the Hector MotorWorks Facility Gamma on Hector, turning out the design for their own touman as well as for broader Clan use. Clan Ghost Bear maintained a separate facility on Bearclaw, which supplied the Ghost Bear touman and those of allied Clans throughout the Succession Wars and Clan Invasion periods.

The Clan Invasion brought the Mithras into contact with Inner Sphere forces, where the design proved well-suited to the fast-paced flanking operations that Clan commanders favored in conquered occupation zones. The Fire Mandrill Kindraa Kline accumulated a notable concentration of the vehicles, having captured a number of tanks from Clan Ice Hellion following the Ice Hellions' failed Hellion's Fury campaign against their Clan rivals. The Kindraa's Twenty-first Vanguard Cluster found the design well-matched to their defensive doctrine, using the tanks to fix and harass enemy positions while Elemental forces maneuvered to deliver the decisive blow.

The Ghost Bear facility on Bearclaw transferred to the Rasalhague Dominion during the Civil War, and then to Clan Star League forces during the Jihad period, reflecting the political upheaval of the era. The Hector facility changed hands as well, passing from Clan Ice Hellion to Clan Goliath Scorpion during the Jihad, before Clan Coyote ultimately assumed control in the early Dark Age. Engineers at the Hector facility developed the ERLL variant during the Jihad period, substantially upgrading the vehicle's long-range firepower to meet the demands of the changed operational environment.

The Mobile Headquarters is the original dedicated command vehicle of the Star League Defense Force, designed and manufactured by Star League Defense Industries on Mars beginning in 2620. For over a century, the Mobile HQ served as the nerve center of large-scale planetary operations, gathering information from ground forces, aerospace assets, and orbiting spacecraft to present a comprehensive battlefield picture to the commanding officer. The vehicle changed little during its production run, evidence of the soundness of its original design. Its destruction during the Amaris Coup and the subsequent loss of replacement technology made surviving examples among the most prized military assets in the Inner Sphere.

A typical Mobile HQ is divided into two main sections. The communications room seats up to six operators with standing room for twelve more, dominated by a TriHolo table at its center that displays surrounding terrain, individual troop positions, and known enemy formations in three-dimensional detail. The sophisticated battle computer tied into the table can project future movements and suggest courses of action based on whatever variables the commander enters. Three communications stations allow the commander and a staff of seven commtechs to maintain constant contact with forces in the field. The powerful transmitters are capable of piercing most jamming systems and can connect to distant JumpShips using a collapsible main array mounted on the roof.

A complex dynamic suspension system keeps the interior stable, allowing normal activity within despite the vehicle's speed on rough terrain. A single turret-mounted Defiance B3M medium laser provides minimal self-defense, reflecting the vehicle's intended position well behind the front lines. StarSlab/4 armor provides adequate protection against light weapons and shrapnel. The TharHes HQ CommSet and Diplan-IX SideSweeper targeting system round out the electronics package, though many surviving examples have lost some or all of these systems to age and battle damage.

Star League Defense Industries produced the Mobile HQ on Mars for over a century, equipping every major SLDF formation with at least one of these sophisticated command platforms. The vehicle became so integral to large-scale operations that its loss could cripple a command's ability to coordinate forces across a planet. When Stefan Amaris launched his coup in 2767, the SLDI factory on Mars was destroyed, ending production permanently. No other manufacturer possessed the technical expertise to replicate the vehicle's advanced electronics suite.

The Succession Wars proved catastrophic for the remaining Mobile HQ fleet. The vehicles were prime targets for capture or destruction, and those that survived often suffered irreparable damage to their electronics. By the early thirty-first century, most surviving examples were only partially functional, with working computers or TriHolo tables replaced by more conventional tracking methods. Some vehicles were gutted entirely, their functional equipment transplanted into smaller command vans to preserve at least some coordination capability. Others had their fusion engines stripped and sold to keep light BattleMechs operational, receiving internal combustion engines as replacements. When Wolf's Dragoons appeared in the Inner Sphere, they were notable for possessing five seemingly brand-new and fully operational Mobile HQs, a fact that astonished military observers across every Successor State. As Star League technology became available again during the technological renaissance, efforts were made to restore surviving vehicles, gradually increasing the number of operational Mobile HQs in service.

The Mobile Long Tom stands among the most feared indirect-fire weapons in the Inner Sphere, a rolling siege battery capable of reducing fortifications and destroying armored formations from distances that place its crews entirely beyond the reach of retaliation. Built by Rebel Industrial Technologies, Inc. of Mars and introduced in 2602, the design was conceived for the Star League Defense Force as a mobile decisive fire-support option capable of breaking any fixed defense without exposing assault troops to unnecessary risk.

Taking the form of a convoy of up to six tracked vehicles centered on an Armstrong Industries Long Tom Rifle Mobile Chassis System, the Mobile Long Tom converts a weapon of immense destructive power into a self-sufficient mobile battery that can relocate after firing to deny counterbattery response. When the Star League collapsed and these systems passed to Successor States forces, their fearsome reputation only grew during the brutal wars that followed. Few weapons have so consistently shaped the calculus of defensive warfare across three centuries of Inner Sphere conflict.

The Mobile Long Tom achieves its destructive power through extreme range and raw hitting power rather than any pretension toward survivability. The convoy's centerpiece is the Armstrong Industries Long Tom Rifle Mobile Chassis System, an artillery piece with a reach measured in kilometers that is equally suited to destroying fixed fortifications, disrupting massed formations, and systematically demolishing urban terrain. Four SperryBrowning machine guns provide minimal close-range defense against infantry but offer no meaningful protection against combat vehicles or BattleMechs. The crew depends entirely on supporting arms for anti-aircraft and anti-armor coverage.

Power comes at a significant cost in mobility. The Robel 110 ICE engine provides road movement capability but precludes cross-country travel when the full convoy is assembled, and the ICE power plant demands constant refueling. Three ammunition carriages carry approximately seventy-five rounds in total, enough for just over four minutes of continuous fire before the battery must reposition to await resupply. StarSlab/1 armor protects the crew from small arms and artillery fragments but cannot withstand dedicated anti-vehicle fire. A single pass by a hostile aerospace fighter or an unsupported flanking BattleMech can destroy the entire system. The Mobile Long Tom's survivability depends entirely on concealment, distance, and the vigilance of its escorts.

The Mobile Long Tom predates the height of the Star League itself. Rebel Industrial Technologies introduced the design in 2602 at their Mars facility, constructing it as a mobile fire support platform for the Star League Defense Force's expanding campaign requirements. While most armies fielded conventional artillery in fixed emplacements or towed configurations, the SLDF demanded a weapon capable of relocating after firing, denying counterbattery response and maintaining offensive momentum during extended campaigns. The resulting LT-MOB-25 satisfied that demand by concentrating everything necessary for sustained bombardment into a convoy of tracked vehicles that could be broken apart, moved independently, and reassembled within hours.

The Mobile Long Tom found its first major institutional role as part of the Terran Hegemony's Main Guardian Defense System. Rather than station permanent SLDF ground forces on every world lacking a Space Defense System, the Hegemony equipped major population centers with networks of automated Guardian drone tanks controlled by central computers, supported by Mobile Long Tom batteries to provide the decisive firepower those drones could not carry. When the SLDF undertook its liberation campaign during the Amaris Civil War, those computers and their drone complements were methodically destroyed to prevent the enemy from recapturing them. The Mobile Long Tom batteries survived, left behind as isolated fire support assets whose doctrinal purpose had been eliminated along with the systems they once supported.

When the Star League dissolved and the Exodus stripped the Inner Sphere of its finest military minds and most advanced technology, the Mobile Long Tom proved both too valuable and too simple to abandon. Rebel Industrial Technologies continued production on Mars through the first century of the Succession Wars under successive periods of Rim Worlds Republic and later ComStar stewardship, keeping artillery batteries operational across every major power. The system's simplicity was its principal advantage: ICE power plants, conventional munitions, and uncomplicated electronics that could be maintained with Succession Wars-era industrial capacity.

The history of the Mobile Long Tom is written in the rubble of the cities it has bombarded. In 2888, Draconis Combine forces raiding the Davion world of Errai discovered that two Mobile Long Toms firing from an urban position could neutralize an entire raiding force before it could establish a defensive perimeter, their rounds dismantling cover and forcing a withdrawal rather than face sustained bombardment. On Berenson, a prolonged engagement between House Marik and House Liao saw each side's batteries hunting the other for nearly a week, with espionage and sabotage ultimately determining the outcome. In 3002, a Marik strike against Treth in the Lyran Commonwealth turned on the defenders' decision to use a single Mobile Long Tom to simulate a larger battery, successfully deceiving the attackers into a premature withdrawal before their objectives were secured.

These engagements reinforced a doctrine that placed Mobile Long Tom batteries at the core of garrison and defensive planning across all major powers. Batteries of four to six units attached to regimental battle groups controlled the ground around any fixed position with the implicit threat of fire from kilometers in any direction. The psychological weight of artillery is disproportionate to its mechanical specifications. Soldiers unable to see what is destroying them, hearing only the distant concussion before impact, fight differently than those facing direct fire.

The LT-MOB-25F, introduced in 2695, extended the system's capabilities with ferro-fibrous armor, CASE protection, and a more powerful engine that improved road speed. Multiple manufacturers took on production, including Bithinian Ballistics, Lycomb-Davion IntroTech, Austen-Armstrong Industries, and Taurus Territorial Industries, dispersing the design's production base across multiple factions. When the Jihad silenced the Mars facility, those dispersed production lines ensured continuity. The 3132 Blackout demonstrated that indirect fire remained among the few weapons capable of neutralizing the agile OmniMechs favored by raiders, driving a post-Blackout production revival across the Inner Sphere. The LT-MOB-95, introduced by the Federated Suns in 3097, rationalized the entire system into a single compact chassis through Kallon Weapon Industries, eliminating the convoy requirement and the logistical burden it had always imposed while preserving the Long Tom's fundamental destructive reach.

shared: The Moltke Main Battle Tank is a seventy-five-ton fusion-powered tracked combat vehicle developed by Brooks Incorporated for the Duchy of Andurien during the Jihad, entering production in 3076. Commissioned directly by the Duchy to address critical equipment shortfalls without relying on outside suppliers, the Moltke was designed to provide local armored forces with a capable frontline vehicle drawing on the structural philosophy of the ancient Augustus A-3. Brooks retained the Augustus's distinctive triple-turret arrangement and sloping track guards while replacing the old diesel powerplant with an extralight fusion engine and fitting the design with modern heavy ferro-fibrous armor and advanced electronics. The result was a tank that offered considerably greater speed, firepower, and survivability than its Age of War ancestor while maintaining a visual continuity that tied the new design to the Duchy's established manufacturing identity. The Moltke rapidly became the Duchy's primary armored asset during and after the Jihad period.

The Moltke is powered by a Vlar 300 XL fusion engine, reaching a top speed of approximately sixty-four kilometers per hour and reducing crew requirements to five compared to the Augustus A-3's ten. StarSlab/7 Heavy Ferro-Fibrous armor provides substantial protection for its weight class. A Maxell 650 communications system paired with a Maxell TA 85 targeting computer incorporating TAG allows the Moltke to serve as an artillery spotter in addition to its direct-fire role, giving combined-arms formations a vehicle capable of directing indirect fire assets from the front line.

The M1's turret carries a Diverse Optics Sunbeam extended-range laser flanked by two Imperator Automatic Weaponry light Gauss rifles, concentrating long-range precision firepower in the triangular mount inherited from the Augustus. Three tons of rifle ammunition support sustained engagements. The M2 trades this long-range combination for close-support capability, replacing the main laser with a Snub-Nose PPC and adding five multi-missile launchers at the vehicle's front with six tons of ammunition, providing exceptional short-range saturation fire and ammunition flexibility. The M3 retains the triangular turret but replaces the light Gauss rifles with a pair of Kali Yama Weapons Industries LB 10-X autocannons with cluster and standard ammunition options, supplemented by a FlameTech Inferno plasma rifle for anti-infantry and anti-stealth work and TAG for artillery coordination. The M3's biggest weakness, shared across all variants, is a lack of dedicated anti-infantry weapons beyond the plasma rifle's area effect.

The Moltke's development began as a direct response to the pressures of the Jihad, when the Duchy of Andurien found itself stretched by the demands of sustaining forces without reliable access to outside supply chains. The Word of Blake's disruption of interstellar commerce and the broader chaos of the conflict left many smaller powers scrambling for indigenous solutions, and the Duchy turned to Brooks Incorporated to produce a modern heavy tank that could be built and maintained entirely within Duchy space. Brooks drew on the legacy of their Age of War Augustus A-3, retaining its structural character while bringing the design fully into the modern technological era.

The M1 entered production at Andurien in 3076, with initial output distributed among militia forces and Free Worlds League regulars stationed in the Duchy. Outside parties inquired early about purchasing the Moltke for their own forces, and Brooks forwarded these requests to Duchy government offices for approval, establishing a pattern of controlled export that would define the tank's distribution through the Jihad period. The M2 variant followed in 3077, intended to complement the M1's long-range precision fire with heavier short-range capability, giving combined-arms formations a more flexible armored component. The M3 arrived in 3080, incorporating lessons from Jihad-era engagements, particularly the value of TAG designation for artillery coordination and anti-infantry systems in an environment increasingly complicated by battle armor and stealth-equipped infantry.

Following the Jihad's conclusion, distribution expanded cautiously beyond Duchy forces. Sales opened to the Principality of Regulus and the Duchy of Oriente, with the M1 and M2 seeing the broadest export uptake. The Duchy declined to authorize sales outside former League worlds that were not politically aligned with Andurien interests, keeping the Moltke's distribution concentrated within the remnants of the Free Worlds League sphere. The tank's single production facility at Andurien remained active through the Dark Age under Duchy of Andurien oversight, sustaining output for a design that had become the backbone of Duchy armored formations.

Sungdong-STX Shipbuilding, a Terra-based firm with centuries of experience constructing fast-hulled surface vessels, designed the Moray Heavy Attack Submarine in 2635 for the Star League Defense Force. Contracted to provide the SLDF's Royal CAAN regiments with a heavily armed undersea fire support platform, Sungdong-STX drew on its expertise in submersible cargo vessel construction to create a formidable 140-ton submarine. The Moray was designed to operate in partnership with the lighter Manta Fast Attack Submarine, providing the heavy firepower and durability that its companion lacked. The pairing gave CAAN regiments a flexible undersea combat team capable of responding to threats across multi-hundred-kilometer engagement zones. The Moray earned a reputation as one of the most formidable conventional submarines in the Inner Sphere, capable of engaging targets ranging from enemy submersibles to surface vessels.

The Moray was built to absorb punishment and deliver devastating torpedo salvos. Its Electro-Motive 390 XL fusion engine provides a maximum flank speed of 54 kilometers per hour, considerably slower than the Manta but adequate for a vessel designed to hold position and fight rather than conduct hit-and-run attacks. The engine consumes nearly a quarter of the submarine's 140-ton displacement, a significant investment that provides extended mission duration and reliable power for the vessel's extensive weapons suite.

Eighteen tons of AquaTec ArmorSlab ferro-fibrous armor give the Moray exceptional survivability for a submarine of its class. CASE protection prevents ammunition detonations from destroying the vessel outright, a critical feature given the large torpedo magazines carried aboard. The hull provides comprehensive coverage across all aspects, allowing the Moray to endure sustained engagements that would quickly overwhelm lighter submarines.

The weapons fit is extensive and well-distributed. The bow mounts twin Sea Devastator twenty-tube long-range torpedo launchers alongside a Sea Harvester six-tube short-range torpedo launcher. A dorsal turret carries an additional ten-tube long-range torpedo launcher, a short-range torpedo launcher, and a pair of Averell Poseidon extended-range medium lasers. Stern-mounted launchers eliminate blind spots in the engagement envelope. Three tons of ammunition per long-range launcher type and four tons for the short-range systems provide reasonable endurance for extended patrols, though the Moray's ammunition dependency remains its primary operational constraint.

Sungdong-STX Shipbuilding developed the Moray in 2635 as the heavy partner to the planned Manta fast attack submarine. At the height of the twenty-eighth century, Sungdong-STX operated facilities across a dozen Hegemony worlds producing submersibles ranging from bulk cargo vessels to underwater aerospace carriers. The Moray represented the firm's response to an SLDF requirement for a heavily armored support submarine capable of anchoring undersea combat teams in contested waters.

The Moray served with distinction in CAAN regiments throughout the Terran Hegemony. During the Amaris Civil War, Moray crews fought in defense of Terra's oceans, though the conflict exacted a heavy toll on the submarine fleet. The Succession Wars proved fatal to the design's continued service. Advanced components required for the extra-light engine and ferro-fibrous armor became irreplaceable as the technological base of the Inner Sphere collapsed, and the last operational examples were decommissioned by ComStar after it assumed control of Terra.

The Word of Blake's seizure of Terra brought the Moray back from extinction. Sungdong-STX's production lines were reactivated alongside Royal Nelson's Manta facility as part of the Blakist program to field Wyrm SDS Submersible Fortresses. New Morays entered service as escorts for these massive underwater weapons platforms, operating in their traditional paired role with newly built Mantas. The Blakists upgraded the original laser armament to extended-range models during reactivation, the only meaningful change to the decades-old configuration.

After Terra's liberation in 3079, surviving Morays joined the Coalition effort to neutralize rogue Wyrm platforms still under Blakist control. The Republic of the Sphere retained both the design and Sungdong-STX's production capability, continuing to build new hulls to support underwater command infrastructure and the remaining Wyrm fortresses under Republic authority.

The Morningstar City Command Vehicle is a 60-ton wheeled combat vehicle representing the second major joint venture between General Motors of Kathil and Ceres Metals Industries of Tikonov. Designed from inception as a city command vehicle (CCV) capable of coordinating combined-arms maneuvers in the absence of BattleMechs, it serves as the command hub and companion unit to the lighter Minion hover tank.

The C³ master computer at the heart of the Morningstar's design defines its battlefield purpose, making it the nerve center of any urban formation it joins. The partnership between General Motors and Ceres Metals that produced both the Morningstar and the Minion was unlikely to survive the political upheavals of the FedCom Civil War, and the Morningstar stands as the final product of that collaboration.

The Morningstar is powered by a VOX 280 XL fusion engine, giving the 60-ton vehicle a respectable cruising speed for its class. Nine tons of Durallex Standard armor provides solid protection, particularly suited to the urban environments where the CCV was designed to operate. The vehicle is not intended for extended independent campaigns, carrying limited ammunition, but its cargo bay can be configured to transport a squad of battle armor troops or a standard infantry platoon, adding tactical flexibility to its command role.

Primary armament is a Mydron Excel Autocannon 10, which delivers consistent firepower against armored targets at moderate range while the vehicle maintains its command posture. Three Slingshot Machine Guns provide close-range point defense against infantry and light vehicles in densely built-up areas. The Morningstar is not engineered for extended independent action, and a lone Morningstar stripped of its network is a comparatively modest threat.

The Overlook J11 communications system integrates a C³ master computer, the central reason for the vehicle's existence. This system allows the Morningstar to coordinate a full Command/Control/Communications net, linking BattleMechs and subordinate vehicles through shared targeting data across an entire command company. The Brightstar 17 Mk. II targeting system is shared with the Minion, a deliberate design choice ensuring full compatibility across the combined-arms team. Without its C³ net, the Morningstar loses much of its battlefield value and becomes dependent on its autocannon and point defense weapons alone.

The Morningstar was developed in the final stages of design at General Motors' Kathil plant, conceived as a city command vehicle to lead urban defensive operations. Its development ran parallel to that of the Minion, with both designs emerging from the same joint venture. While the Minion provided front-line combat capability, the Morningstar supplied command authority, and the two were intended from the outset to operate as an integrated pair. The second joint effort between General Motors and Ceres Metals Industries, the Morningstar reflected a deepening cooperation between the two manufacturers in the years before the FedCom Civil War made that collaboration untenable.

The FedCom Civil War validated the city command vehicle concept under live-fire conditions. Morningstars led urban assaults across multiple contested worlds, coordinating mixed lances of tanks and infantry to seize smaller cities and production sites while BattleMechs contested the major capitals. The Federated Suns fielded most of the extant Morningstars during the civil war period, deploying them extensively on Kathil and Tikonov. House Liao expressed significant interest in acquiring the design, and Capellan intelligence obtained enough production data from Tikonov to support eventual independent production at the Warlock facility. When Capellan forces retook Tikonov, the production line was redirected to supply Confederation formations.

During the Jihad, the Tikonov facility briefly operated under independent management before passing to Republic of the Sphere control. The Kathil line remained continuously under Federated Suns ownership, maintaining a reliable supply of Morningstars into the Dark Age period. Both the Federated Suns and the Capellan Confederation separately pursued upgraded designs featuring dual C³ master computers, reflecting the high value both states placed on the command vehicle concept. The Word of Blake also adapted the Morningstar platform into a specialized mobile communications hub during the Jihad, producing limited numbers at Tikonov for their own operational requirements.

The Morrígú's primary armament consists of two Series 1 extended-range large lasers and two Type XV "Crossbow" LRM-15 launchers, all mounted in a turret for full traverse. This configuration delivers concentrated fire at extended range and reflects the Blood Spirits' long-standing preference for direct energy weapons, a philosophy evident across multiple Blood Spirit designs including the Blood Kite. Mounting all primary weapons in the turret allows the Morrígú to engage targets at any bearing without repositioning the hull, a useful capability given its limited ground speed.

For close defense, a Pattern J1 SRM-2 launcher is mounted on each flank, covering threats that close inside the main engagement envelope. A Consolidated Type 2M ECM suite adds electronic protection, complicating enemy targeting solutions. Both the communications and targeting systems are Consolidated products, providing reliable electronics performance.

The Morrígú carries thirteen tons of Compound JX4 armor, more substantial than most Clan combat vehicles at this weight class. However, the Fusion 240 powerplant produces a top speed of only 54 km/h, limiting tactical flexibility considerably. This vehicle is designed for static fire positions at range rather than mobile engagements. Commanders who rely on the Morrígú in fluid situations where the battle line shifts quickly will find its pace a genuine liability. It carries no jump jets, and repositioning under pressure offers no quick solution.

The Morrígú was commissioned in the early 3060s by Khan Karianna Schmitt of Clan Blood Spirit, intended as a visible assertion of continued strength in the aftermath of the Absorption War. Alongside the Crimson Langur OmniMech and the ongoing ProtoMech development effort, the vehicle was one of several projects meant to signal that the Blood Spirits remained capable of fielding competitive military hardware.

Khan Schmitt chose the vehicle's name personally. Her Welsh heritage was held in near-sacred regard among the Blood Spirits, tracing lineage directly to Colleen Schmitt, the Clan's founding Khan. Colleen Schmitt had descended from Colonel Hanni Schmitt, the last commander of the Royal Black Watch Regiment of the Star League, a lineage treated as nearly holy within Blood Spirit culture. Drawing on that ancestry, Khan Karianna Schmitt chose a name from Celtic mythology: the Morrígú, a goddess of war said to appear wherever battle was joined. The name was a deliberate statement of purpose.

Production at the York Vehicle Y2 Facility on York began in 3064, and the vehicle was distributed across every Galaxy in the Blood Spirit Touman, including the newly established Iota Galaxy: Retribution. A complete Star of Morrígú vehicles appeared within the Twenty-second Combat Force, a Trinary formed by Kindraa Mick-Kreese of Clan Fire Mandrill, signaling the strengthening bond between the Blood Spirits and their Crusader-aligned neighbors in the Homeworlds. That the vehicle found favor with the most fanatically Crusader of the Kindraa factions was seen as fitting, given the Blood Spirits' own Crusader leanings.

The Wars of Reaving ultimately destroyed Clan Blood Spirit as a political entity. Before the York facility was lost, however, Clan Diamond Shark had acquired the production plans. In 3068 the Sharks established the New York Vehicle Y2 Facility on Trondheim, named explicitly in reference to its predecessor. Where the original production served the Blood Spirits exclusively, the Trondheim facility operated as a commercial venture, making the Morrígú available to any buyer. During the Jihad, the facility suffered significant personnel losses but maintained production at reduced capacity, and it carried the design forward through the Dark Age and into the ilClan era under Diamond Shark, and later Sea Fox, stewardship.

The Musketeer Hover Tank was developed by Corean Enterprises of New Avalon and entered service with the Armed Forces of the Federated Suns in 3065. Designed as a dedicated rotary autocannon platform, it arrived during a period of intense interest in RAC-based weapons systems across the Federated Suns. Corean engineers prioritized speed, sustained firepower, and operational economy, producing a hover tank capable of delivering rapid, concentrated damage across a wide range of engagements. Its combination of high cross-terrain mobility, continuous autocannon output, and solid crew protection made it attractive for both offensive strike roles and screening operations. The Musketeer became one of the first production vehicles to fully exploit RAC technology at scale, establishing Corean Enterprises as a leading supplier for the AFFS ground forces and earning a reputation as a cost-effective frontline combat vehicle.

The Musketeer is built around a single turret-mounted Mydron Tornado Rotary AC/5, fed by a substantial three-ton magazine that sustains fire well in excess of one minute at maximum rate. This endurance distinguishes the Musketeer from lighter autocannon designs and gives it exceptional battlefield persistence. For close-range engagements, a pair of Holly Mark II Streak SRM 2-Packs provide accurate secondary fire without wasting ammunition on missed shots. A forward-fixed TAG designator rounds out the weapon suite, allowing the crew to direct guided artillery support onto targets without closing to weapon range.

Propulsion comes from a GM 115-rated internal combustion engine, enabling a top speed approaching 120 kilometers per hour on flat terrain with a cruising range of nearly 1,500 kilometers on standard combustible fuels. Seven tons of StarGuard CIV ferro-fibrous armor provide protection sufficient to withstand a hit from the heaviest standard autocannon. An integrated CASE system shields the crew from catastrophic detonation of ammunition or fuel, addressing the particular vulnerability of ICE-powered vehicles to internal fires.

The Musketeer's primary limitation is its dependence on the single RAC main gun. A jam or mechanical failure at a critical moment leaves the vehicle with only the Streak launchers for close-in defense. The hover chassis, while fast on open ground, loses much of its mobility advantage in heavily wooded terrain, dense rubble, or steep gradients, restricting the design's effectiveness in urban and forested environments.

The Musketeer emerged from the Federated Suns' rapid embrace of rotary autocannon technology following its development in the early 3060s. As RAC weapons spread through the Inner Sphere, manufacturers throughout the Federated Suns moved quickly to incorporate the new systems into both BattleMech and vehicle designs. Corean Enterprises secured the contract for the Musketeer in 3065, introducing the design to the AFFS as political tensions within the Federated Commonwealth were reaching a critical threshold.

The timing proved consequential. The Musketeer entered full production only months before the FedCom Civil War erupted, and the design found itself in combat on both sides of the conflict almost immediately. Corean Enterprises' facility on New Avalon placed it at the center of the fighting, with Musketeer units participating in the final battles for the planet itself. This early combat exposure on both sides of the Civil War cemented the design's battlefield reputation and generated significant demand for expanded production.

Following the Civil War, the AFFS moved to consolidate control over the Musketeer's production run, securing an exclusive five-year contract with Corean Enterprises and prioritizing militia units on worlds facing the Draconis Combine and Capellan Confederation. An armor-enhanced configuration, the (Armor) variant, entered service in 3068, offering commanders the option of trading burst-fire capability for improved vehicle survivability. By the time of the Jihad the Musketeer had become a well-established element of Federated Suns ground forces, deployed across multiple commands and proving itself effective in the sustained attritional combat of that era.

A further modernization produced the (3080 Upgrade) configuration, refining the design's systems based on accumulated field experience from both the Civil War and Jihad. The upgrade extended the Musketeer's operational life into the Dark Age period. Production of all variants continued on New Avalon under Federated Suns ownership through most of the Republic era, with the New Avalon facility eventually transitioning to Draconis Combine control following the collapse of the Republic of the Sphere.

The Myrmidon Medium Tank entered production in 3060 as a New Earth Trading Company initiative to meet rising demand for affordable tracked firepower in an increasingly unstable Inner Sphere. Taking its name from legendary Greek warriors, the tank was designed from the outset as an accessible alternative to heavier, costlier BattleMech units. Drawing on the proven Manticore platform as a conceptual baseline but built around a more economical power plant, the Myrmidon delivers long-range firepower competitive with lighter BattleMechs at a fraction of the acquisition cost.

NETC marketed the design primarily to smaller state militias and independent commands unable to maintain full BattleMech forces, making the Myrmidon a fixture of Chaos March and periphery battlefields from the Civil War era into the thirty-second century.

The Myrmidon is a 40-ton tracked medium tank built around a Nissan 200 fusion engine, yielding a road speed of 86 km/h and a cross-country pace of 54 km/h. That performance falls short of hover alternatives and lighter wheeled designs, but the tracked suspension delivers reliable mobility across a wide range of terrain conditions. The Myrmidon carries no jump capability.

Firepower centers on a single turret-mounted Parti-Kill Heavy Cannon, a particle projection cannon providing long-range striking power equivalent to the primary armament of many medium BattleMechs. A SureShot Mk VI SRM-6 rounds out the turret, adding close-range punch against infantry and lightly armored targets. The combined loadout allows engagement at multiple ranges, though the SRM system carries limited ammunition for sustained operations.

Protection comes from an ArcShield Maxi II standard armor suite. Coverage is adequate for a medium design but leaves the Myrmidon vulnerable to concentrated fire from heavier opponents. The fusion engine eliminates the catastrophic ammunition explosion risk present in combustion-powered vehicles, a selling point for smaller militaries with limited maintenance facilities. The reduced crew requirement compared to older medium tanks eases manpower demands, though it limits situational awareness during sustained combat.

NETC developed the Myrmidon in the late 3050s in direct response to rising demand for affordable combined-arms firepower in the Chaos March and across the broader Inner Sphere. The collapse of the Federated Commonwealth and the ongoing Clan threat had left dozens of smaller worlds and independent commands scrambling for military equipment they could afford and maintain. NETC's engineers reviewed the successful Manticore chassis and chose to produce a lighter, less expensive alternative rather than compete in the heavier tank market. The decision to accept a more modest power plant was explicitly commercial, not tactical.

Initial production at New Earth supplied primarily the Lyran Alliance, which was fortifying its Clan invasion corridor in the late 3050s and early 3060s. A portion of NETC output went to independent militaries throughout the Chaos March, where the Myrmidon quickly earned a solid reputation in low-intensity conflicts against Capellan-backed guerrilla forces. The practical economics of the design attracted consistent mercenary interest, and NETC established a steady export market through the Civil War period.

Jalastar Aerospace, a Federated Suns manufacturer best known for its Manticore production on Panpour, entered a licensing agreement with NETC during this period to produce the standard Myrmidon for AFFS contracts. The arrangement complicated Jalastar's internal sales priorities, given the Myrmidon's overlap with their Manticore line. Jalastar's engineers would later leverage their familiarity with the design to develop a substantially modified anti-infantry variant.

The Jihad proved catastrophic for original Myrmidon production. Word of Blake forces assaulted New Earth in the mid-3070s, and the fighting effectively destroyed NETC's manufacturing capacity on the planet. With the original production line gone, the Maxwell Planetary Defense Consortium approached NETC in the mid-3080s about acquiring a production license. NETC accepted the arrangement, and Maxwell began producing the Myrmidon at their facility on Maxwell around 3088, securing the design's continued availability into the Republic era and beyond.
